text:
tara: Noticed a sustained host CPU tail on streaming pool after the kernel picker tweak this morning. p95 host CPU +16% on parse-heavy hosts.
yves: saw the same alerts. only during long-lived streaming sessions where responses are chunked/sent incrementally.
samir: timeline? which tweak rolled?
tara: rolled kernel-selector v1.3.2 at 08:05 UTC to prefer the 'opt-window' kernel for mid-length sequences. spike starts ~08:12 and shows up on ~22% of nodes.
infra-bot: deployment: kernel-selector v1.3.2 -> streaming-group-canary / 3/8 -> SUCCESS
trace-bot: quick flame sample from affected host:
parse_assemble         32.4%
kv_prefix_lookup       14.2%
tokenize_stream        13.8%
http2_frame_read       9.9%
syscall_read_small     6.1%
other                  23.6%

yves: interesting that http2_frame_read and small syscalls are noticeable. suggests more small reads from the socket, maybe windowing behavior changed.
samir: could kernel change affect how we batch outgoing tokens which then changes incoming chunk boundaries? If sequence pacing differs, fragment alignment against cached prefixes could break.
tara: digging into packet traces: after kernel change, we see smaller gRPC payloads per chunk - average chunk size down ~22 bytes. KV cache hit rate dropped from 98.6% -> 90.7% during incident window.
yves: smaller payloads -> more frequent reads -> higher per-read decode cost due to hpack. Also tokenizer sees repeated normalization calls for prefixes that aren't reused.
samir: repro harness I used:
```
./streambench --model=fast-chat --clients=14 --mean-msg=150 --chunk-avg=110 --duration=5m
```
I toggled kernel selector back to previous version locally and saw CPU tail disappear.
tara: quick mitigations: 1) rollback kernel-selector on streaming pool 2) bump kvcache prefix grace to 300ms for canary 3) enable socket read buffering option we experimented with last quarter for two hosts.
yves: did canary TTL bump already. after TTL=300ms on 2 hosts, p95 CPU dropped ~7% and kvcache hit returned to ~95% on canary.
samir: can we instrument a tracer flag when kernel-selector picks 'opt-window' kernel and add chunk-size histograms to telemetry? Need to correlate kernel choice -> chunk size -> kvcache reuse.
tara: agreed. also small code change: tokenizer fast-path to bypass utf8-normalize when bytes are valid ASCII without control characters. I'll open a tiny PR.
yves: also add a gating rule: kernel selector changes must run paired emit-shape canaries measuring chunk CDF and prefix reuse before wide rollout.
samir: followups: tara will open tokenizer PR and rollback if canary doesn't improve; yves to add chunk-size hist metric + kvcache prefix reuse gauge; samir to add trace tag for kernel path. infra-bot: queued rollback plan.
tara: thanks all - keeping watch on the rollback window. :white_check_mark:
